newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf Air in $100mln loan talks.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Air in $100mln loan talks.

text.p: Gulf Air officials are negotiating with its owners to raise a $100 million loan to rescue the debt-ridden regional airline, a weekly in the United Arab Emirates reported on Sunday.

Al-Eqtisadi said Qatar, one of the four owners, was reluctant to participate in the optional loan, but did not elaborate. Bahrain has asked the UAE's Abu Dhabi government to contribute on its behalf, it quoted informed sources as saying.
Gulf Air officials were not immediately available yo comment on the report.
"Qatar is still showing reluctance to participate in the optional loan," the magazine quoted one source as saying.
"Bahrain, which faces difficulty in raising its contribution to the loan, has asked Abu Dhabi to finance its share in the proposed loan and consider it as a loan to Bahrain," he said.
The airline's board in January asked the owners -- Abu Dhabi, Oman, Qatar and Bahrain -- to extend loans to the company to ease its cash crunch.
Abu Dhabi had offered to pump in fresh capital and loans to help the airline, but the offer was opposed by Oman and Qatar, fearing the move will give Abu Dhabi control over the airline.

The weekly quoted the sources as saying Abu Dhabi had also opposed an offer by Qatar to buy Bahrain's and Oman's shares in the airline, fearing that such a move would deal a blow to the economy in Bahrain, where the airline is based.
Officials had said Gulf Air faced $2 billion in debts resulting from lavish buying of costly aircraft on loans and opening numerous uneconomic routes in the 1980s.
Gulf Air is the national carrier for the four owner states. Qatar and Oman have also their own cariers also.
In 1995, the company closed its books with $159 million losses and was unable to service its loans. It has not yet issued the financial results for 1996.
